question: Assign seven staff members (Person 0 to Person 6) to three projects (Project 0, Project 1, and Project 2) such that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project. Each project has specific skill requirements: Project 0 requires a skill level of 8 for Skill 0 and 8 for Skill 1, Project 1 requires a skill level of 7 for Skill 0 and 9 for Skill 1, and Project 2 requires a skill level of 9 for Skill 0 and 7 for Skill 1. Each staff member has specific skill levels: Person 0 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 1 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 2 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 3 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 4 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, Person 5 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, and Person 6 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7. The attained skill level for each project is the sum of the skill levels of the assigned staff members. The skill shortage for each project is the difference between the required skill level and the attained skill level. The goal is to minimize the maximum skill shortage across all projects and skills. Constraints include ensuring that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project, and that the skill shortages for Project 0, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 0, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 1, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -7, for Project 1, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -9, for Project 2, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -9, and for Project 2, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -7.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "people": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "projects": [0, 1, 2],
    "skills": [0, 1],
    "person_skill": {
        (0, 0): 5, (0, 1): 7,
        (1, 0): 6, (1, 1): 7,
        (2, 0): 5, (2, 1): 7,
        (3, 0): 6, (3, 1): 7,
        (4, 0): 5, (4, 1): 6,
        (5, 0): 5, (5, 1): 6,
        (6, 0): 5, (6, 1): 7,
    },
    "project_required": {
        (0, 0): 8, (0, 1): 8,
        (1, 0): 7, (1, 1): 9,
        (2, 0): 9, (2, 1): 7,
    },
    # "the skill shortages for Project 0, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -8, ..."
    "shortage_upper": {
        (0, 0): -8, (0, 1): -8,
        (1, 0): -7, (1, 1): -9,
        (2, 0): -9, (2, 1): -7,
    },
    "big_M": 1000.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["people"])
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["projects"])
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=d["skills"])
    model.JS = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(j, s) for j in d["projects"] for s in d["skills"]],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # x[p,j] = 1 if person p is assigned to project j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, model.J, within=pyo.Binary)

    # shortage[j,s] = required - attained (can be negative when over-staffed)
    model.shortage = pyo.Var(model.JS, within=pyo.Reals)

    # z = maximum shortage across all (project, skill) pairs
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Reals)

    # Each staff member assigned to exactly one project.
    def assign_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.x[p, j] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.assign_once = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=assign_rule)

    # Shortage definition: shortage = required - sum_p skill[p,s] * x[p,j]
    def shortage_rule(m, j, s):
        attained = sum(d["person_skill"][(p, s)] * m.x[p, j] for p in m.P)
        return m.shortage[j, s] == d["project_required"][(j, s)] - attained
    model.shortage_def = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=shortage_rule)

    # z upper-bounds every shortage (max-shortage definition)
    def max_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.shortage[j, s] <= m.z
    model.max_bound = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=max_rule)

    # Explicit shortage upper bounds from the problem text.
    def explicit_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.shortage[j, s] <= d["shortage_upper"][(j, s)]
    model.explicit_bound = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=explicit_rule)

    # Objective: minimise the maximum shortage.
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.z, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

    # "shortage <= negative" forces an unattainable surplus and makes the

        (1, 0): -7, (1, 1): -9,
        (2, 0): -9, (2, 1): -7,
    },
